newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. capital area sees rising school enrollment.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. capital area sees rising school enrollment.

text.p: The region around New York state's capital, Albany, likely will see the number of schoolchildren rise for the next five to 15 years, before the trend reverses by 2020, Albany Times Union said.
While public schools rely heavily on local property taxes for funding, such revenues usually fall short, requiring the state to fund the rest of their budgets.

The paper, citing data compiled by the Capital District Regional Planning Commission, said the picture is mixed for some districts, as Shenendehowa and Watervliet, for example, which will see enrollment level off and even decline by 2000.
In contrast, the number of school children in Guilderland and Ballston Spa is expected to keep growing.

While New York City is having great difficulty finding space for its students, with the system at nearly 10 percent above cpacity, the state's total enrollment at 2.86 million is only expected to rise 1.2 percent over the next 10 years.
In its Thursday edition, the paper said the biggest increase is projected for grades 9 to 12, with the autumn 1996 enrollment of 844,000 seen rising by 116,000 in 2006.
